Having RGB controlled via PCIe is usually a pretty dirty hack that I am glad to not see on this card. A common implementation is using SMBus, which is a fairly low level bus between system devices on your motherboard. Gigabyte for instance does this using a fucking KERNEL MODE DRIVER that FULLY EXPOSES the bus. Even without administrator access. Unsuprisingly, the software commonly gets flagged by anticheat, commonly causes bluescreens, has been causing bios resets for some people, and adds a huge security flaw to your system. 

Long story short, having PCIe for the GPU and seperate, independent USB for RGB is secure and harmless. Its just a much cleaner implementation software wise even if it means extra cables. Its also going to work for pretty much anyone.

If you look at the hardware architecture specs for the A770, is has more of pretty much everything compared to the 3060Ti. More ROP (128 vs 80), more texture units (256 vs 152) and more media engines (4x the media throughput of the single NVENC engine in the 3060Ti). The two media engines in (vs the 1 in the RTX) also support AV1 encode, where the RTX 3000 series don't. All of those things take up die space, they don't come for free.
